title: Quotient formula for extension along an invertible scalar map
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a symmetric monoidal closed category with equalizers and coequalizers, in which tensoring on either side preserves colimits. Let $R,S$ be commutative monoid objects ([sk-def-sfb-ring-object]) and $\varphi:R\xrightarrow{\sim}S$ an isomorphism of monoid objects. Module objects and their morphisms are those of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Use restriction, extension and coextension of scalars as in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. For an $R$-module $N$ with action $\gamma_N:R\otimes N\to N$, put $T_N=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi^{-1}}N$; its underlying object is $N$ and its $S$-action is $\beta_N=\gamma_N\circ(\varphi^{-1}\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)$. Write $\eta_S:\mathbf1\to S$ for the unit and $\lambda_A:\mathbf1\otimes A\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ for the left unitor.

Let $F_N=\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}N=S\otimes_R N$, with coequalizer map $q_N:S\otimes N\to F_N$. The action $\beta_N$ coequalizes the two maps defining $F_N$. The component $p_N:F_N\xrightarrow{\sim}T_N$ of the adjoint-uniqueness comparison of [def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso] is the unique factor satisfying
$$p_N\circ q_N=\beta_N.$$
Its inverse has underlying morphism
$$s_N=q_N\circ(\eta_S\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)\circ\lambda_N^{-1}:N\to F_N.$$
With the $S$-action of $T_N$ on the domain of $s_N$, both $p_N$ and $s_N$ are $S$-linear, and
$$p_N\circ s_N=\mathrm{id}_{T_N},\qquad s_N\circ p_N=\mathrm{id}_{F_N}.$$
The $p_N$ and $s_N$ are natural in $R$-module morphisms $N\to N'$. Thus the extension comparison is normalized by its value on the coequalizer map, and its inverse is insertion of the unit followed by that coequalizer map.

source.place: Proof, last sentence: the two comparisons through restriction along the inverse; explicit component normalization of def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso

proof.text:
Put $\psi=\varphi^{-1}$, $I=\operatorname{Res}_{\psi}$ and $H=\operatorname{Res}_{\varphi}$. By [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], $I(N)=T_N$ has action $\beta_N$ and both restriction functors keep underlying morphisms. For an $S$-module $M$ with action $a_M$, the linearity equation of [det-def-sfb-module-objects-definition] for a map $h:N\to M$ is
$$h\gamma_N(\psi\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)=a_M(\mathrm{id}_S\otimes h).$$
Precompose with $\varphi\otimes\mathrm{id}_N$, or conversely with $\psi\otimes\mathrm{id}_N$, to see that this is equivalent to
$$h\gamma_N=a_M(\varphi\otimes h).$$
Consequently $\operatorname{Hom}_S(I(N),M)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,H(M))$, $h\mapsto h$, is a bijection. It is natural in both variables: precomposition and postcomposition on either side are the very same underlying compositions.

source.place: Composite restriction formula and identity on underlying morphisms; explicitly write the identity Hom bijection for inverse restriction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] to step 1 to obtain $b:I\dashv H$. Its unit at $N$ is the image of $\mathrm{id}_{I(N)}$, so its underlying morphism is $\mathrm{id}_N$. Indeed, the action on $H(I(N))$ is $\gamma_N(\psi\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)(\varphi\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)=\gamma_N$ by [def-sfb-modobj-restriction]. Likewise the counit is an underlying identity. This is the canonical inverse-restriction adjunction: the inverse restrictions cancel through the identity maps, rather than an arbitrary rescaling of the adjunction.

source.place: Tag 0037, definition-adjoint and the following unit/counit formulas; apply to the identity Hom bijection of step 1.

proof.text:
The hypotheses of [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction] hold: $\mathcal C$ is braided with coequalizers preserved by tensoring and $R$ is commutative. It supplies $a:\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}\dashv H$ with unit
$$u_N=q_N(\eta_S\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)\lambda_N^{-1}.$$
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to $a,b$, with identical right adjoint $H$ and $\delta=\mathrm{id}_H$. The resulting natural isomorphism $p:\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}\xrightarrow{\sim}I$ is characterized by $H(p_N)\eta_{a,N}=\eta_{b,N}$. This is the comparison of [def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso] named in the statement. That comparison is the one of [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] for $a$ and the adjunction $b':I\dashv H$ given by the left-adjoint clause of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-inverse-adjoint], applied to the equivalence $H$ with quasi-inverse $I$ of [def-sfb-modobj-restriction-equivalence]; the unit of $b'$ is $\beta^{-1}$ for the equivalence isomorphism $\beta:HI\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$, whose components have identity underlying morphisms (both facts belong to the construction that the statement names). So the unit of $b'$ and the unit of $b$ from step 2 have the same underlying morphisms. By [det-def-sfb-module-objects-definition], module morphisms are their underlying morphisms, so the units agree. The formula $\Psi(f)=H(f)\circ\eta$ of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] then shows that $b'$ and $b$ have the same Hom bijections, so $b'=b$. The two comparisons are therefore the same. On underlying objects the unit equation is
$$p_Nu_N=\mathrm{id}_N.$$
The components $p_N$ are $S$-linear isomorphisms, since this comparison is a natural isomorphism between functors valued in $S$-module objects.

source.place: The two adjunctions and their unique compatible comparison; unit normalization is the cited conjugate-isomorphism equation (Stacks Tag 0B65).

proof.text:
Write $a_F:S\otimes F_N\to F_N$ for the action on the extension. The statement of [def-sfb-modobj-extension] says that this action is induced by multiplication on the first factor, namely
$$a_F(\mathrm{id}_S\otimes q_N)=q_N(\mu_S\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)\alpha_{S,S,N}^{-1}.$$
Substitute the displayed formula for $u_N$. Naturality of $\alpha$ and the right-unit identity $\mu_S(\mathrm{id}_S\otimes\eta_S)=\rho_S$ of [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid] give
$$\begin{aligned}
a_F(\mathrm{id}_S\otimes u_N)
&=q_N(\mu_S\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)\alpha_{S,S,N}^{-1}(\mathrm{id}_S\otimes(\eta_S\otimes\mathrm{id}_N))(\mathrm{id}_S\otimes\lambda_N^{-1})\\
&=q_N(\rho_S\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)\alpha_{S,\mathbf1,N}^{-1}(\mathrm{id}_S\otimes\lambda_N^{-1})=q_N.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is the monoidal triangle axiom $(\rho_S\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)\alpha_{S,\mathbf1,N}^{-1}=\mathrm{id}_S\otimes\lambda_N$. Thus no calculation with elements or assumed tensor generators is involved.

source.place: Extension action through multiplication on S, composed with insertion of its unit; expand the right-unit and monoidal triangle axioms.

proof.text:
By the module-morphism equation of [det-def-sfb-module-objects-definition], $p_Na_F=\beta_N(\mathrm{id}_S\otimes p_N)$. Combining steps 3 and 4 yields
$$p_Nq_N=p_Na_F(\mathrm{id}_S\otimes u_N)=\beta_N(\mathrm{id}_S\otimes(p_Nu_N))=\beta_N.$$
Let $d_0,d_1:(S\otimes R)\otimes N\rightrightarrows S\otimes N$ be the defining pair in [def-sfb-modobj-extension]. Since $q_Nd_0=q_Nd_1$, the formula just proved gives $\beta_Nd_0=p_Nq_Nd_0=p_Nq_Nd_1=\beta_Nd_1$. Finally [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], applied to this finite parallel-pair diagram, says that there is exactly one underlying morphism $F_N\to N$ whose composite with $q_N$ is $\beta_N$. It is $p_N$.

source.place: Unit formula and extension action, giving the value of the comparison on the quotient; uniqueness by Stacks Tag 002F, definition-colimit.

proof.text: The proposed $s_N=q_N(\eta_S\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)\lambda_N^{-1}$ is exactly $u_N$ as an underlying morphism. Thus step 3 gives $p_Ns_N=\mathrm{id}_{T_N}$. As $p_N$ is invertible, $s_N=p_N^{-1}(p_Ns_N)=p_N^{-1}$, whence $s_Np_N=\mathrm{id}_{F_N}$. The inverse in step 3 is already an $S$-module morphism, so $s_N$ is $S$-linear for the action $\beta_N$ on its domain. This uses the module category of [det-def-sfb-module-objects-definition], whose composition and identities are the underlying ones.

source.place: Unit insertion is the inverse of the unit-compatible comparison: compose the unit equation with its already established inverse.

proof.text:
For an $R$-linear $h:N\to N'$, [def-sfb-modobj-extension] defines $E(h)=\operatorname{Ext}_{\varphi}(h)$ by $E(h)q_N=q_{N'}(\mathrm{id}_S\otimes h)$. The module-morphism equation in [det-def-sfb-module-objects-definition], precomposed with $\psi\otimes\mathrm{id}_N$, gives $h\beta_N=\beta_{N'}(\mathrm{id}_S\otimes h)$. Hence
$$h p_Nq_N=h\beta_N=\beta_{N'}(\mathrm{id}_S\otimes h)=p_{N'}E(h)q_N.$$
Uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] cancels $q_N$, giving $h p_N=p_{N'}E(h)$; by [def-sfb-modobj-restriction], $I(h)$ has underlying map $h$. Naturality of tensoring and of the left unitor also gives directly
$$E(h)s_N=q_{N'}(\mathrm{id}_S\otimes h)(\eta_S\otimes\mathrm{id}_N)\lambda_N^{-1}=q_{N'}(\eta_S\otimes\mathrm{id}_{N'})\lambda_{N'}^{-1}h=s_{N'}h.$$
These are both asserted naturality equations.

source.place: Definition of extension on morphisms, and inverse restriction on the same underlying morphisms; write both naturality equations.
